summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of Crohn’s disease and multiple prior abdominal surgeries was admitted with abdominal pain and diarrhea consistent with a disease flare. Initial labs showed acute kidney injury, dehydration, and nongap metabolic acidosis, all secondary to fluid loss from diarrhea. CT imaging revealed fecal loading and mild stranding in the distal ileum, improved from prior studies, with no obstruction or hernia. He was treated with IV fluids, increased prednisone to 40 mg daily, and supportive care. His symptoms improved, labs normalized, and he tolerated a regular diet. Stool studies ruled out infection. He was discharged home on continued prednisone, a short course of pain medication, and instructions to follow up with gastroenterology.
problems: Adrenal cortical steroids causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
